claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and still living at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a 17-year-old son named Alex living at home with you.

Since Alex is 17 (over 16), an important factor for Child Benefit eligibility is whether he's in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Since Alex is 17 and studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, that counts as approved education.

Now I need to understand your living situation and responsibility for Alex. Let me ask:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Now I need to ask about your income situation, as this can affect Child Benefit:

**Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year?**

(This won't affect your eligibility to receive Child Benefit, but it may mean you'd need to pay a tax charge on it.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - is that something I need to know to find out if I'm eligible? I just want to know if I can actually claim it for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're absolutely right - I apologize for any confusion! The income question relates to a potential tax charge, but it doesn't affect whether you're **eligible** to claim Child Benefit in the first place.

Let me ask the key eligibility question: **Are you responsible for Alex - meaning you live with him and/or pay for his upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me and I take care of all his needs - food, clothes, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just confirm one more thing:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, his other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 17 and in approved education (studying for his A-levels at sixth form college)
- You live in the UK
- You live with Alex and are responsible for his upkeep
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

Since Alex is studying for his A-levels, you can continue to claim Child Benefit for him until he turns 20, as long as he remains in approved education or training.

**Important note:** Your Child Benefit will stop if Alex:
- Starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education
- Starts an apprenticeship in England
- Starts claiming certain benefits in his own right (like Universal Credit)

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If your circumstances change, make sure to inform HMRC.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
